cards.text: The Sadducees just took their shot at Jesus with a question about the resurrection, and He silenced them (Matthew 22:23-33). So the Pharisees, another group of Jewish religious leaders, gather together. One crew walks off the field quiet, and the next crew is already stretching on the sideline like, “Put me in, coach!”

cards.question: One of the Pharisees steps up to test Jesus with a question. Who is he?

cards.text: This isn't a friendly chat. It's a test: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?” Out of the WHOLE Law, pick ONE. No pressure!

cards.question: Out of the whole Law, which commandment does Jesus call the first and greatest?
Heart, soul and mind. In the greatest commandment, Jesus is talking about loving God with ___ of you.

cards.text: Jesus answers with a command from God's Law: “Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.” He calls it “the first and greatest commandment.”
The man asked for ONE commandment, and Jesus says there's a second one just like it. Friend, that's me when a baker asks for my one best baking tip and I hand them TWO. What can I say? I'm a giver!

cards.question: Jesus says the second commandment is like the first one. What is it?

answers.text: Give to your neighbor in need

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says these two commandments, loving God and loving your neighbor, are small next to the rest of the Law.

cards.text: Jesus says, “All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.” Picture that one hook by your front door holding every coat, every bag and every set of keys you own, and now picture somebody pulling it out of the wall. EVERYTHING hits the floor.
The Pharisees are still gathered, and now Jesus asks them: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” The guys who came with the questions are now the ones in the hot seat.

cards.question: Jesus asks whose son the Christ is. The Pharisees answer that He is the son of ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus points them to something David, Israel's king, said in the Spirit. David says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

cards.question: Jesus asked the Pharisees about the Christ, then quoted King David. In David's line, who is the one David calls “my Lord”?
Jesus asks the Pharisees, “So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?” What makes that so hard to answer?

answers.text: David would be calling his own son Lord
David would be calling an enemy his Lord
David would be calling a stranger his Lord

cards.text: Jesus leaves that question hanging over the Pharisees: King David calling his own son ‘Lord.’ That's like the CEO standing up when the new hire walks in and saying, “After you, BOSS.”

cards.question: True or false: The Pharisees come right back at Jesus with a sharp answer to His question about David's Lord.
Nobody can answer Jesus a word. From that day on, what does no one dare to do?

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "This isn't a friendly chat." / "It's a test: ...?" / "Out of the WHOLE Law, pick ONE." / "No pressure!" Only the opening card may run past 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. Cards 4 and 5 already asked about the greatest commandment and established it (Matthew 22:37-38). Card 6 then retells the same verses, which moves the passage nowhere. Fold the BSB quote into a setup card before card 4, or cut this card.
This story card has four sentences: "The man asked for ONE commandment..." / "Friend, that's me when..." / "What can I say?" / "I'm a giver!" Only the opening card may run past 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Jesus leaves that question hanging over the Pharisees" tells the baker the Pharisees have no answer. That gives away card 17, which asks whether they come right back with a sharp answer (Matthew 22:46).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It restates card 15's answer ("King David calling his own son ‘Lord’") and cites Matthew 22:45 again without moving the passage forward. Only the joke is new.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
